job: List posts, releases or resources as rows, cards or one lead entry, filtered and paged.
purpose: list: ruled rows (a date rail, or without one the kind, title, summary, authors and a small frame). grid: media (the signature texture, a typographic cover or a picture in fd-site-media), title, meta. featured: one large entry beside a short list. The whole item is the link. As a listing, entries carry data-kind and data-tags, a tools bar of existing controls filters them, a live count follows, and site.js pages them and can keep the filters in the address.
useWhen: A few recent posts or releases on a landing page, linking to the full list.
A blog index, a resources library or a news page: 10 to 60 entries filtered by kind and topic and paged.
Past issues of a newsletter with Show more.

avoidWhen.when: The versioned release notes in the documentation.
A feed of activity in the app.

states.name: filtered
states.how: a control with data-filter changed: non-matching entries get hidden and .fd-site-posts-count says "12 of 30 resources"

states.name: no results
states.how: nothing matches: the .fd-empty after the list is shown, with a [data-clear] button

states.name: paged
states.how: data-page-size on the section: an empty .fd-pagination is filled, or a button[data-more] shows the next page

states.name: in the address
states.how: data-address: ?kind=&topic=&q=&page= follow the listing and Back restores it

states.name: loading
states.how: the page swaps the entries for skeletons and disables the tools; the count says what is loading

variants.useWhen: Releases and posts where the date matters.
One post that leads, and a few more.

parts.role: Its title; the link covers the item.
Its frame: an image or the signature texture.
An entry's kind label (Report, Guide, Engineering).
The format line: authors, date, reading time, "PDF · 24 pages".
A document's cover drawn in type in the media frame; data-ground="inverse|raised".
The tools bar: chip nav or tabs, a select, a search, the count.

keyboard.does: The tools are the existing chip nav, select and search; page buttons move focus to the first entry of the new page.
